name: Hard Reset
subtitle: The 1997 Album (The First on Engine Room Records)
linerNotes: If The Warehouse Tapes was the band surviving, Hard Reset is the band conquering.

As the inaugural release on their own label, Engine Room Records (ERR-001), this album had everything riding on it. Industry insiders predicted a flop without Apex's marketing machine. Instead, fueled by a grassroots "Direct-to-Fan" internet campaign engineered by Holly, the album debuted at #1, proving you didn't need to sell your soul to sell out stadiums.
description: If The Warehouse Tapes was the band surviving, Hard Reset is the band conquering.

studioArchives.title: The $13.99 Price War
studioArchives.content: In 1997, major labels were charging $18.99 for a CD. Because Engine Room Records owned their own pressing plants and distribution, Holly priced Hard Reset at a flat $13.99—and printed the price directly on the front cover sticker so retailers couldn't mark it up.

studioArchives.title: The Sound of "The Engine"
studioArchives.content: This is the first album where the "Stardust" (Cassidy's synths) and the "Engine" (Ryan's heavy guitars) are mixed at dead-even volume. The result is the signature "Industrial Arena Rock" sound that defined the band's second decade.
